events.title: Investor visa implementing decree registered by the Corte dei conti
events.description: The inter-ministerial decree of 21 July 2017 (Economic Development, Interior, Foreign Affairs) on the investor visa procedure was registered by the Court of Auditors on 17 August 2017 (reg. prev. n. 778). It sets up the 7-member Committee (MISE chair; Interior; Foreign Affairs; Financial Intelligence Unit; Guardia di Finanza currency police; Revenue Agency; ICE), with Culture or Education ministry members added for donations, and requires the Committee to adopt an operating manual at its first meeting, to be called within one month.
events.quote: REGISTRATO ALLA CORTE DEI CONTI- UFFICIO CONTROLLO ATTI MISE E MIPAAF IN DATA 17 AGOSTO 2017, REG.NE PREV. N. 778.

events.title: Investor Visa Committee approves the operating manual
events.description: At its founding meeting on 16 November 2017 the Investor Visa Committee approved the operating manual required by the decree of 21 July 2017; from then the programme is called 'Investor Visa for Italy'. The manual was updated by the Committee on 19 July 2021.
events.quote: approvato in sede di riunione istitutiva dal Comitato per l’attuazione del visto investitori, come previsto dallo stesso DI, il 16 novembre 2017

events.title: Investor Visa for Italy operating manual updated
events.description: The Committee updated the operating manual on 19 July 2021, incorporating the 2020 changes (applications on behalf of foreign legal persons under art. 40-quater D.L. 76/2020; 5-year exemption from the integration agreement).
events.quote: Il manuale è stato aggiornato dal Comitato il 19 luglio 2021.

events.title: Investor Visa Committee members appointed
events.description: A decree of the MISE Directorate-General for industrial policy (DGPIIPMI) of 14 November 2017 named the members of the Investor Visa Committee.
events.quote: Il Decreto del DGPIIPMI del MISE del 14 novembre 2017 individua i membri del Comitato.

events.title: Anti-money-laundering decree repeals the investor visa FIU pre-check clause
events.description: D.Lgs. 25 May 2017, n. 90 (anti-money-laundering reform, G.U. 19 Jun 2017) repealed comma 4 of art. 26-bis (preliminary checks with the Financial Intelligence Unit to be completed within 15 days). Date is the Gazzetta publication date given in the amendment history; the in-force date is not stated there.
events.quote: ha disposto (con l'art. 8, comma 14) l'abrogazione del comma 4 dell'art. 26-bis.

gaps: The ministry publishes no investor visa statistics after 31 Dec 2021 in these documents; the 2022 report covers only the start-up route (9 applications), and approvals for all routes are not printed in either report.

ledger.contains: MIMIT web page on Investor Visa for Italy (captured 2026-10-02; footer 'last update 10 Oct 2018' although it lists the 2020 amounts): programme open to non-EU citizens since December 2017; 2-year visa; four routes with minimum amounts (EUR 2m government bonds, EUR 500k Italian company, EUR 250k innovative start-up, EUR 1m philanthropic donation); online, bilingual, centralised procedure with clearance within 30 days; legal references; responsible office. Taken as rules (6 rows). No statistics. Page rating '4.5 / 5' is a web-page feedback score, not programme data.

Inter-ministerial decree of 21 July 2017 (6 pp.) implementing art. 26-bis: purpose; definitions (eligible government bonds with at least 2 years residual maturity, Italian-resident companies, innovative start-ups, philanthropic donations); the Committee (7 members, plus Culture/Education ministry for donations; clearance votes need no votes against) and its Secretariat; required documents (incl. criminal records for 10-year lookback); procedure (decision within 30 days, permit request within 8 days of entry, proof of investment within 3 months, 2-year permit, 3-year renewal, revocation if divested); roles of ministries; manual to be adopted within a month; Corte dei conti registration 17 Aug 2017. Taken: 8 rules and 1 context event (the decree itself is already an event). No statistics.

English home page of the Investor Visa for Italy portal (captured 2026-10-02): 2-year visa; four thresholds (EUR 2m bonds, EUR 500k limited company, EUR 250k innovative startup, EUR 1m philanthropy); two notices suspending the programme for Russian and Belarusian citizens (Committee chair order 14 Jul 2023) and for dual nationals with a Russian or Belarusian passport (MAECI note 20 Mar 2024), both already events. Taken: 5 rules. No statistics.

Investor Visa for Italy operating manual, version of 19 July 2021 (29 pp.): legal basis and history (manual first approved 16 Nov 2017, updated 19 Jul 2021); definitions (2-year permit renewable for 3 years; eligible applicants incl. legal representatives of foreign legal persons; four investment types, one investment only, none made before applying; company must be active and have filed at least one balance sheet); application documents (bank statements, origin of funds, criminal records with 10-year lookback, passport valid 2 years 3 months); Secretariat and Committee procedure (7 or 8 members, voting rules, roles, decision within 30 days, 30-day suspensions); clearance valid 6 months; consular appointment (income above about EUR 8,500); entry, permit within 8 working days, permit fees EUR 30.46 + 50.00 + EUR 16 stamp; investment within 3 months and proof documents; maintenance and renewal (60 days before expiry). Taken: 18 rules and 2 events. Not taken: Italy's flat-tax regime for new residents described on pp. 5-6 (EUR 100,000 a year, EUR 25,000 per family member, up to 15 years, 9 of 10 prior years non-resident) because it is a separate tax regime, not this programme; Industria 4.0 plan (EUR 18 billion) and Italia Startup Visa (2014) context. No statistics.

MIMIT annual report to Parliament on start-up and innovative SME policy, 2022 edition (83 pp.). Investor visa content only in summary point 19 (p. 9) and section 2.4.1 (pp. 78-79): programme description (from 16 Nov 2017; 2-year permit, 3-year renewals; four thresholds; 30-day decision; free application; Committee of 7 or 8), and start-up-route applications to 31 Dec 2021: 9 in total (already in), by nationality (CHN 3 already in; GBR 2, ARE, LBY, COL, AUS 1 each added; parts sum to 9), by start-up city (Milan 7 = 77%, Rome 1, Novara 1), by sex (1 F, 8 M), by education (4 bachelor, 2 master, 2 high school, 1 doctorate; sums to 9), outcomes (6 investments completed, 2 rejected already in, 1 closed for non-arrival; sums to 9); sectors listed without numbers. Rules: 6 rows. Rest of the report (start-up register, Italia Startup Visa 527 applications, Startup Hub, tax incentives, funds) is about other policies and out of scope.

MISE annual report to Parliament on start-up and innovative SME policy, 2020 edition (2019 data, 87 pp.). Investor visa content in the executive summary (p. 12), section 1 box (p. ~19) and section 6.7 (pp. 76-77): description, thresholds (EUR 2m bonds, EUR 1m donations, EUR 500k company, EUR 250k start-up; halving by D.L. 34/2020 in footnote 62), Committee members named by decree of 14 Nov 2017, manual 16 Nov 2017, portal 14 Dec 2017 (already an event); applications to Dec 2019: 13 total, 6 rejected, by route 8/2/3 and nationality RUS 3, ISR 2, CHN 2, SYR 2 (all already in), plus KOR, TUR, BRA, ARE 1 each (added); parts sum to 13 both ways; amount per application by route ('ciascuno'). 'All accepted investments took place' has no number (approvals not printed). Section 7 recap of D.L. 34/2020 art. 38 repeats the halving. Rest of the report (start-ups, Italia Startup Visa/Hub, CLab, incentives) is out of scope.

D.L. 34/2020 (Decreto Rilancio) art. 38, original text: commi 1-9 and 11-19 are start-up support measures (EUR 100m Smart&Start, EUR 10m grants, EUR 200m venture-capital fund, tax deductions of 50% up to EUR 100,000, First Playable Fund EUR 4m, costs EUR 314m etc.), out of scope. Comma 10 halves the investor visa thresholds for companies (EUR 1m to 500k) and innovative start-ups (EUR 500k to 250k): both rules and the event are already in the tables. Nothing new to add.

Art. 40-quater D.L. 76/2020 (added on conversion by L. 120/2020, in force 15 Sep 2020): investment may be made on behalf of a foreign legal person the applicant legally represents, with a reciprocity check by the Foreign Ministry (new commi 3-bis, 3-ter); holders get the rights of the self-employment permit, are exempt from the reciprocity check and, for five years from first issue, from the integration agreement and continuous-stay obligations (new comma 5-bis). Event already in; the 5-year exemption added as a rule.

L. 193/2024 (annual competition law 2023) art. 35: rewrites art. 26-bis(1)(b) to add Italian venture-capital funds to the EUR 500k route; start-up threshold EUR 250k restated; editorial note reproduces art. 26-bis(1) as amended (EUR 2m bonds, EUR 1m donation, proof of funds EUR 2m / EUR 1m, 3-month deadline). Company/VC rule and event already in; 6 rules added from the article and the note.

Art. 26-bis of the immigration consolidated act as in force on 1 Jan 2017 (inserted by L. 232/2016): entry outside annual quotas for investors with EUR 2m government bonds, EUR 1m company / EUR 500k innovative start-up, EUR 1m donation (already in); proof of funds EUR 2m / EUR 1m; investment within 3 months; 2-year holding; implementing decree within 90 days; documents; FIU pre-checks within 15 days (comma 4, later repealed); 2-year permit, 3-year renewals; family reunification; 1.5-6 years prison for false documents. Added 8 rules; launch event already in.

Current art. 26-bis (in force since 18 Dec 2024): four routes (EUR 2m bonds; EUR 500k company or Italian VC fund; EUR 250k innovative start-up; EUR 1m donation), investment possible for a represented legal person, proof of funds EUR 2m / EUR 1m, 3-month investment deadline, 2-year holding, documents, reciprocity check (3-bis, 3-ter), comma 4 repealed, 2-year permit, 5-year exemption from integration agreement (5-bis), 3-year renewals, family members, 1.5-6 years prison for false documents. Added 12 rules (none were stored from this version).

Normattiva list of the six acts that amended art. 26-bis with Gazzetta dates: L. 232/2016 (21 Dec 2016, insertion), D.Lgs. 90/2017 (19 Jun 2017, repeal of comma 4), D.L. 34/2020 (19 May 2020, comma 1(b)), D.L. 76/2020 (16 Jul 2020) as converted by L. 120/2020 (14 Sep 2020; commi 1, 3-bis, 3-ter, 5-bis), L. 193/2024 (17 Dec 2024, comma 1(b)). All but the D.Lgs. 90/2017 repeal are already events from the acts themselves; that one added as an event. No numbers.
